text:
**LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most people.** Most current power stations use it, and the sources agree on why.

| | LiFePO4 | NMC |
|---|---|---|
| Rated cycle life | Roughly 2,000-6,000 cycles | Roughly 500-1,000 (some sources say up to 2,000) |
| Failure behavior | Milder: lower peak temperatures, less gas | More violent: hotter, flames in lab tests |
| Weight | Somewhat heavier per Wh | Lighter at the cell level |
| Price | Median about $0.55/Wh in one dataset | About $0.95/Wh in the same dataset |

- **Cycle life:** This is the biggest difference. Daily cycling, such as in a van or off-grid, would wear out a 500-cycle NMC battery in about 1.4 years, versus about 8 years for a 3,000-cycle LFP one ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). For a few outages a year, cycle life barely matters for either chemistry ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- **Safety:** In lab tests, LFP cells peaked at much lower temperatures than NMC cells (about 259°C vs 731°C in one study) ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). LFP is not fireproof, though. One test found it reached thermal runaway earlier in overcharge ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)), and the DOE notes LFP systems have had incidents too ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- **Weight:** NMC cells are denser, but the gap mostly shrinks in finished products because the inverter, case, and fans weigh the same either way. In same-maker pairs, the LFP version was only a little heavier per kWh ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). Compare actual spec sheets instead of assuming.
- **Cold weather:** Chemistry matters less than you'd think. Most stations of either type won't charge below 32°F ([PowerStations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Check the manual for your model.
- **Cost:** The price premium for LFP has largely disappeared. Per rated cycle, LFP is far cheaper ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).

**When NMC could make sense:** a small, lightweight unit you'll carry and use rarely, or a heavily discounted older unit. If you already own a working NMC station, keep using it.

**Buying tips**
- Check the spec sheet for the chemistry. Some pages say only "lithium-ion."
- Compare cycle ratings by their end point too. "3,000 cycles to 80%" promises more than "4,000 to 70%."
- Pick the size and output for what you need to run first, then use chemistry as the tiebreaker.
